claims.statement: All oxyromon state lives in a single SQLite file `oxyromon.db` inside the data directory (`OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY`, else `dirs::data_dir()/oxyromon`), created on demand and opened by `establish_connection`; tests open a `tempfile::NamedTempFile` through the same function, so a test database is a production database with migrations applied.

`establish_connection` splits pool shape on the Cargo feature set with `cfg_if`: a default CLI build gets max_connections=1 with `PRAGMA locking_mode = EXCLUSIVE`, while a build with `server` or `mcp` gets max_connections=5 with `locking_mode = NORMAL`, because long-lived web/MCP servers must multiplex requests and must not hold the file exclusively.

Before any query runs, `establish_connection` issues `foreign_keys = ON`, `journal_mode = WAL`, `synchronous = NORMAL`, `temp_store = MEMORY`, `mmap_size = 268435456`, `cache_size = 10000` and `auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL` on the pool, and `foreign_keys = ON` is what makes every schema cascade (system deletion, romfile detachment) actually happen; each failure panics.

Migrations are embedded at compile time as `static MIGRATOR: Migrator = sqlx::migrate!()` and `MIGRATOR.run(&pool)` executes on every connection setup including tests; a failing migration panics, so there is no version negotiation, no down-migration and no way to run against a half-applied schema.

`optimize_database(pool)` runs `incremental_vacuum`, `optimize` and `wal_checkpoint(truncate)` and itself acquires a pooled connection, which is why the CLI dispatch scope must release its connection first; it pairs with `auto_vacuum = INCREMENTAL` to return freed pages at the end of a run.

The schema splits declaration from reality: `systems`/`games`/`roms` record what a DAT says should exist (name, expected size, crc/md5/sha1, merge status) while `romfiles` records files actually on disk, joined only by `roms.romfile_id ... ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting a file row detaches rather than destroys the ROM declaration and `romfile_id IS NULL` means wanted-but-unmatched.

Uniqueness is scoped per parent rather than global: `systems.name` and `romfiles.path` are globally unique, `games` is unique on `(name, system_id)`, `roms` on `(name, game_id)`, `patches` on `(name, rom_id)`, and `headers` on `(system_id)` (one header per system); romfiles.path uniqueness lets `import_rom` skip an already-registered file unless `--force`.

Parent/child structures are self-referential foreign keys rather than junction tables: `games.parent_id` (clone to parent), `games.bios_id`, `games.playlist_id` to a `.m3u` romfile (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), `roms.parent_id` (merged-set parent rom) and `romfiles.parent_id` (containing archive, `ON DELETE SET NULL`).

`headers` holds one row per system with the header `size`, and `rules` (split out of `headers` by `20211114103012_create_rules.sql`, which copied and then dropped `start_byte`/`hex_value`) holds the byte signatures; `get_file_and_header_size` counts a file as headered only when all of the header's rules match the bytes at their offsets, otherwise it rewinds and hashes the file whole, and a DAT re-import deletes and re-inserts the whole rule set.

`src/model.rs` maps each table to a plain `#[derive(FromRow)]` struct whose field names match the columns (System, Header, Rule, Game, Rom, Patch, Romfile, Setting), and under `--features server` the same structs additionally derive `SimpleObject`, so GraphQL exposes the row shape directly instead of a separate DTO layer; without the feature the unused fields are `#[allow(dead_code)]`.

`System.games_complete`/`games_total` are not table columns: every System-mapping query appends the same two COUNT subqueries, and `src/query.rs` re-declares that projection as `TableRow::SELECT` for the DataLoader, with a comment requiring the two copies to stay in agreement or the loader cannot map the row.

`Merging`, `Sorting`, `Completion` and `RomfileType` are `#[repr(i8)]` `FromPrimitive` enums persisted as INTEGER/SMALLINT with defaults (merging 0 Split, sorting 0 AllRegions, completion 0 None, romfile_type 0 Romfile); row structs keep the raw `i64` field and call sites narrow with `Merging::from_i64` / `Sorting::from_i64`.

`romfiles.romfile_type` distinguishes ordinary romfiles, generated playlists and patches; the column was backfilled by marking existing `%.m3u` rows as Playlist, but `import_patches` still creates a patch's romfile with `RomfileType::Romfile`, so value 2 is only a label the MCP output layer names 'patch' and never a value the write path produces.

Every query in `database.rs` is a standalone `pub async fn` taking `&mut SqliteConnection` first and returning model types (Vec/Option/single row, i64 count, or `last_insert_rowid()`), using `sqlx::query!` when nothing is mapped and `sqlx::query_as!(Row, ...)` when columns are checked against a struct; because they take a connection not a pool the same functions serve the CLI, the GraphQL resolvers and the MCP read tools.

`begin_transaction`/`commit_transaction`/`rollback_transaction` are thin wrappers over `Acquire::begin` that `expect` success, and since `Transaction<'_, Sqlite>` derefs to the connection the same query functions accept `&mut transaction`; modules open one transaction per unit of work (per DAT, per imported file, per system, per conversion step), and `sort_roms` commits only after the user confirms the planned moves, rolling back otherwise.

Variable-length `IN (...)` lists cannot be macro-expanded, so those queries are string-built and run through `sqlx::query_as::<_, T>(AssertSqlSafe(sql))`, giving up compile-time verification; the same applies to server-side composed SQL in `query.rs` and the MCP read queries, and a few finders exist only under `#[cfg(test)]`.

Query failures panic (`expect` / `unwrap_or_else(|_| panic!(...))` naming the operation and id) rather than returning Result, so a subcommand aborts instead of continuing on a partially-written database; the transactions are what bound the damage. Ids from untrusted clients are the exception: `find_system_by_id_opt` / `find_rom_by_id_opt` return Option and the server turns `None` into a 400.

`systems.completion` and `games.completion` are derived state recomputed by `util::compute_system_completion`, which branches on the system's `arcade` flag and `Merging` mode to pick the SQL game-completion statement, runs the jbfolder statement and then the Wii U `update_nus_games_completion` pass for console systems, and rolls game states up into the system with a CASE; every mutation-heavy subcommand calls it instead of relying on triggers or cached counters.

`romfiles.path` is stored relative to the `ROM_DIRECTORY` setting: writes strip the prefix via `get_relative_path` inside `Persist::create`/`update`, reads rebuild the absolute path in `AsCommon::as_common` with `rom_directory.join(&self.path)`, and migration 20241117210150 rewrote existing rows by stripping the recorded ROM_DIRECTORY prefix, so moving a library is a settings-row update with no table rewrite; the trash query has to match both `%/Trash/%` and the bare `Trash/%` prefix because of it.

`settings` rows carry an optional `system_id`, with uniqueness enforced by two partial indexes (`key` WHERE system_id IS NULL, and `(key, system_id)` WHERE system_id IS NOT NULL); `config::get_setting` reads the per-system row first and falls back to the global row, and all writes funnel through one `upsert_setting` helper, so a system inherits configuration until it overrides it.

Settings values are always text: `config.rs` classifies keys into BOOLEANS, choice/choice-list keys, ranged integers, LISTS, PATHS, NULLABLES and SORTED_LISTS, lists are joined into a single row with `|` (migration 20230528135145 rewrote the earlier `,` separator), and default values are seeded by migrations using `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO settings` — the same statement style used for value retcons such as rewriting RVZ `bzip` to `bzip2`, for the per-format archive compression algorithm/level defaults, and for seeding `PREFER_FORMAT` to NULL so an unset choice means 'no preference'.

The migration workflow is: append `migrations/<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>_<description>.sql`, update the matching `model.rs` struct and `database.rs` queries, then run `cargo sqlx prepare -- --all-targets --features server` to regenerate the committed `.sqlx/` offline query data, and verify with `cargo build --features server`.

The sqlx macros are compile-time verified against the committed `.sqlx/` cache rather than a live database: one JSON file per query, named by the query hash, holding the query text, parameter count and described result columns.

`cargo sqlx prepare` must be run with `--features server` because that feature enlarges the macro query set, and with `--all-targets` so the cached data of test-only queries is kept rather than deleted; CI builds, clippy-checks and tests with `--features server` (plus a separate MCP-without-server clippy pass) so a stale `.sqlx/` cache cannot slip through.

Migration style is dictated by SQLite's limited ALTER TABLE: making a hash column optional is done by rename-add-copy-drop, and adding a constraint or restructuring `settings` means creating a replacement table, copying rows, dropping and renaming.

Index creation is its own migration genre: `(size, crc)`, `(size, md5)` and `(size, sha1)` on `roms` back the hash-matching hot path of ROM import, every foreign-key column gets an explicit index because SQLite creates none, and `games(external_id, system_id)` is a partial unique index that only constrains rows where an external id exists.

`romfiles.parent_id` is a denormalised cache of the parent SHA-1 the CHD format stores inside the child file: `AsChd::parse_chd` reads it in process through the in-tree `chd-rs` crate (`Chd::open` + `chd.info()`, hex-encoding `info.sha1`/`info.data_sha1`/`info.parent_sha1`) rather than parsing external chdman output, which is why the GraphQL `dependencies` resolver reports chd-rs as 'built-in'.

A CHD's parent link is re-verified against the file on every read: `transcode::romfile_as_chd` resolves `romfiles.parent_id` through `find_romfile_by_id` and hands the parent to `as_chd_with_parent`, which re-parses both files and bails with 'Parent CHD SHA1 mismatch' when the cached row no longer matches what the child demands; with no cached link, `as_chd` scans the containing directory for the CHD whose own hash equals the child's `parent_sha1`.

`import_roms` orders candidate import paths by the in-file CHD parent information, processing CHDs that report a `parent_sha1` before parentless CHDs, so a child CHD is matched while its parent is still available.

`find_orphan_romfiles` defines an orphan as a romfile with no `roms.romfile_id` and no `games.playlist_id` referring to it, and deliberately does not consult `romfiles.parent_id`; `purge-roms --orphan` deletes those files and rows in one transaction, and every purge branch (missing, trash, orphan, foreign) ends by recomputing completion for all systems.

`purge-roms --missing` is a disk check rather than a SQL predicate: it reads every romfile row and deletes those whose rebuilt absolute path is not a file, while `--foreign` inverts the lookup by walking the ROM directory and reporting relative paths for which `find_romfile_by_path` returns `None`, sparing update-partition store files that a known WUA still references, and every store file when a known WUA's references can't be read.

`find_romfiles_by_system_id_and_extension_and_no_parent_id` restricts romfiles to a system and extension while excluding rows that already have a parent, so `prompt_for_parent_romfile` never offers a chained CHD as a conversion parent and ranks the remaining candidates by jaro-winkler similarity to the game name.

`convert_roms` treats `find_romfiles_by_parent_id` as a safety guard — it skips a CHD that has child rows — and uses `update_romfile_parent` as the sole writer of `romfiles.parent_id`, setting it to the new parent's id on conversion and clearing it to NULL when a parent is converted away.

The 'wanted ROMs' readers combine `romfile_id IS NULL` with `parent_id IS NULL` (e.g. `find_roms_without_romfile_by_size_and_crc`, `find_roms_without_romfile_by_game_ids`) so a merged child whose data lives in its parent's file is never reported missing, while the PS3/IRD helpers invert that filter (`parent_id = ?` / `IS NOT NULL`) to walk the children of a matched parent.

Arcade completion treats `Merging::Merged` like `Merging::Split`: both run `update_split_games_completion_by_system_id`, which only requires roms with `parent_id IS NULL`, while `NonMerged` runs `update_non_merged_games_completion_by_system_id` and the full strategies require every rom.

The redump.info migration renames twelve Redump systems while preserving their directories by storing the old name as custom_name when none is set, and guards each rename against collisions on both the UNIQUE systems.name column and the unique systems_custom_name index so a collision skips the rename instead of aborting the migration.
The redump.info migration moves every remaining http://redump.org/ system to https://redump.info/ except systems still carrying one of the twelve old names, whose rename was skipped.
purge-games clears `games.playlist_id` itself, setting it to NULL for every game of a playlist once it has moved that playlist to the Trash.
